In the case of Mox(Nb3TaTi3Zr)100−x alloys with a single BCC solid solution phase, the primary strengthening mechanism is solid solution strengthening.

Additionally, fine-grain strengthening also plays a role. Figure 6 illustrates that with the increase in Mo content, the subgrain size decreases. According to the Hall–Petch formula: σs = σ0 + k/D^1/2, the yield strength of the alloy increases as the grain size decreases.
The observed strengthening mechanisms include solid solution strengthening, fine grain strengthening, and precipitated phase strengthening.
